title: The Locust - Wikipedia
notes: Formed in San Diego in 1994 by Justin Pearson, Dylan Scharf, Bobby Bray, Dave Warshaw and Dave Astor as a powerviolence project; first release a split with Man Is the Bastard (1995). Members: Dave Astor drums 1994-2001; Gabe Serbian guitar and vocals 1998-2001, drums 2001 until his death in 2022. The Peel Session recorded in 2001 (released 2010) was 'the first time Gabe Serbian had started playing drums for The Locust', fixing the line-up Bray, Karam, Pearson, Serbian for the rest of the band's life. Genres: grindcore, hardcore punk, powerviolence, mathcore, noise rock; 'grindcore speed and aggression, complexity, and new wave weirdness'; 'abrupt and inconsistent time-signature changes'. Insect costumes in early all-ages shows; 'costumed in skin-tight, full body nylon suits (which the band refer to as uniforms). The last 5 different suits were designed and made by Ben Warwas.' The four stood in a line at the front of the stage, the drums not behind. Dave Lombardo: 'There's a band called The Locust. Their drummer is named Gabe Serbian, and their music hits me now like D.R.I. hit me in the early '80s.' 'Serbian played Ludwig drums with Paiste cymbals.' The band announced on 1 May 2022 that Serbian had died the day before, and later that it could no longer be active.

title: Gabe Serbian - Wikipedia
notes: American drummer and guitarist from San Diego; the Locust, Cattle Decapitation, Holy Molar, Zu, Head Wound City, Le Butcherettes; drummed for Otto von Schirach on a European tour; performed with Alec Empire, Nic Endo, Charlie Clouser and Merzbow. Death given as 29 April 2022 in the infobox and 30 April in the lead's dates; no cause stated.

title: The Locust drummer Gabe Serbian has died, aged 44 - NME
notes: 2 May 2022. Died aged 44; the band said he died on 30 April 2022; no cause given. Joined the Locust in 1998 as guitarist on the self-titled debut, moved to drums in 2001; Cattle Decapitation 1996-2001; Le Butcherettes, Zu, Retox, Holy Molar, Head Wound City. On Plague Soundscapes (2003) and New Erections (2007) and several EPs. Justin Pearson: 'He was the rarest of the rare.'

title: Gabriel Serbian of The Locust - Modern Drummer (Waleed Rashidi, April 2008)
notes: On New Erections (2007, eleven tracks in about twenty minutes). Serbian plays 'wearing a mask that covers most of his face'. 'It usually takes a very long time for us to write a song ... Even when the songs were under a minute ... We'll work out different movements and then we'll figure out how to tie them together.' 'The set list is orchestrated around Serbian's drumming (which is accomplished via an alarmingly simple four-piece Ludwig kit)'. 'I just did it - I never had a plan on how to play like I play ... It just naturally evolves.'

title: Interview with Drummer Gabe Serbian - Big Wheel Magazine (Mindiana Jones, 8 April 2011)
notes: Read through the Internet Archive (the site no longer resolves). Started drumming at 13 in sixth-grade band (clarinet before); a stepfather who was a jazz drummer taught him a rock beat. Influences: 'when I first started playing it was Slayer and Dave Lombardo ... and stuff like Dale Crover ... and various punk bands.' Writes fast parts fast: 'it's usually easier for me to write stuff faster'. Practises only on the kit ('It's always on the set'), no pads or rudiments. Moved from 2B to 5B sticks (Pro-Mark Japanese oak) after Jon Theodore gave him a batch. Admires Kevin Fitzgerald of 400 Blows. The Locust on hiatus with an album's worth of songs.

title: INTERVIEW - Gabe Serbian - Cheap Curls (12 July 2012)
notes: His wife's band's blog. Bands: the Locust, Cattle Decapitation, Skinwalker, Holy Molar, Head Wound City, Retox, Le Butcherettes, Year Future, Wet Lungs, Rats Eyes. 'When I was a kid and decided that I wanted to play drums it was because of the first time I ever heard Slayer ... Dave Lombardo was the reason I started playing drums.' On the tour of Fantomas, the Locust and Trevor Dunn's Trio-Convulsant, he, Lombardo and Ches Smith played together nightly, each soloing over the others' beats. His kit: 'a Ludwig kit from the early 90's ... when Ludwig was first starting to replicate the drums they made in the 70's. Like the really big John Bonham style drums ... my kick drum is a 28" concert bass drum'. Likes vintage Ludwig and Slingerland. Would play in another costume band: 'I'd love to be in Devo or The Residents'. 'My approach to playing drums is usually much more aggressive.'

title: A Day With The Locust - L.A. Weekly (Alec Hanley Bemis, 18 September 2003)
notes: Read through the Internet Archive. The uniforms: 'formfitting full-body suits colored a dingy green ... the material they're made of is rough like unfinished canvas, but skintight like spandex. They have upper-arm vents made of mesh, and holes punched in the hoods covered in the same material. Their mouths and eyes are big fishnet circles.' Bobby Bray: 'All you have to do is listen to how much better Gabe plays blast beats than our old drummer Dave.' Serbian on the blast: 'It's pretty much playing as fast as you can play on everything at once ... I'm doing 16ths on the kick drum and on the snare drum, and that varies with what I'm doing with my right hand and the cymbal.' At a Tijuana show: 'The drums were like lines of dialogue, clearly delineated bursts five seconds long ... muscling through each 16th note like he was laying down a punch'; halfway through the ten-minute set he took off his top, and lifted the mask over his mouth to spit. Brett Gurewitz on Brooks Wackerman's reaction to the band.

title: The Locust's Bugged-Out Debut Made Hardcore Way Weirder - VICE (David Anthony, 26 November 2018)
notes: Pearson and Scharf recruited Dave Astor, Bobby Bray and Dave Warshaw; the powerviolence-indebted early splits; Joey Karam and Gabe Serbian joining made the band. 'Within a few years, the band would bring their bug theme to life by donning increasingly elaborate costumes - or as they preferred, uniforms.' Pearson and Serbian later in Dead Cross, Head Wound City and Retox, with Mike Patton and Dave Lombardo.

title: The Locust (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Gold Standard Laboratories, September 1998; powerviolence, mathcore, grindcore; fifteen songs in under eighteen minutes. Personnel: Justin Pearson, Gabe Serbian (guitar), Joey Karam, Bobby Bray, David Astor (drums).

title: Flight of the Wounded Locust - Wikipedia
notes: Gold Standard Laboratories, 2 October 2001; 'the band's final recording as a five-piece (after which drummer David Astor left and was replaced by then-guitarist Gabe Serbian)'. Personnel: Pearson, Serbian (guitar), Karam, Bray, David Astor (drums). The article carries an unreliable-sources tag.

title: Plague Soundscapes - Wikipedia
notes: ANTI-, 24 June 2003; produced by Alex Newport; 23 songs in 21 minutes; grindcore, noise rock, mathcore, powerviolence; 'a more refined sound than previous The Locust albums, with a greater emphasis on keyboards'. Personnel: Pearson (bass, vocals), Bray (guitar, vocals), Karam (keyboards, vocals), Gabe Serbian (drums). Track 14 is a Crossed Out cover, 'Practiced Hatred'.

title: Safety Second, Body Last - Wikipedia
notes: EP, 11 April 2005, Ipecac / Southern / Radio Surgery; produced by Alex Newport; designed as one ten-minute song in two tracks, each in movements; AllMusic: 'grindy noise with disquieting lulls'.

title: New Erections - Wikipedia
notes: ANTI-, 20 March 2007; produced, engineered and mixed by Alex Newport; the band's third and final studio album; eleven tracks, 23 minutes (AOTKPTA 3:03, Book of Bot 4:31). Personnel: Pearson, Bray, Karam, Gabe Serbian (drums, guitar); Wesley Eisold backing vocals on 4.

title: Cattle Decapitation - Wikipedia
notes: Former members: Gabe Serbian, drums 1996-2001 and lead guitar 1997-2001; Dave Astor, bass 1996-2001 and drums 1997-2003; Michael Laughlin drums 2003-2006. Dates differ between the infobox and the text.

title: Cattle Decapitation - Three One G (artist page)
notes: Formed in San Diego in 1996 with 'David Astor on bass and Gabe Serbian on drums - both of whom were then also members of the Locust'; with Travis Ryan on vocals, 'Astor moved from bass to drums, and Serbian moved from drums to guitar'; Human Jerky and Homovore with that line-up. Serbian left to devote himself to the Locust: 'Serbian now plays drums in the Locust, replacing Astor, who ironically had left the Locust so that he could more fully devote himself to Cattle Decapitation.' Astor later left Cattle Decapitation (Michael Laughlin replaced him).

title: Dave Astor - Drums - Pathology (band site)
notes: Promotional biography: co-founded the Locust in the early 1990s, then Cattle Decapitation, then founded the death metal band Pathology. Puffery; used only for his later bands.

title: RIP Gabe Serbian: 1977-May-1 ~ 2022-April-30 - Patrick Richardson (drum teacher's blog, 3 May 2022)
notes: A drum teacher's appreciation. 'Gabe's mix of jaunty punch-pause-work and cursive flow of rolls across rumbling toms and/or washing cymbals.' His 'traditional 4 piece kit' laid out as an 'obtuse trapezoid': the large rack tom far to the left, the ride dead centre where a rack tom usually is, toms and ride low and flat, both crashes low and close, 'which facilitates his deliciously choppy usage of abruptly choking cymbal-hits with the same hand that hits them'. Points to the Che Cafe overhead footage (c. 2008) and the 2021 House of Blues set ('Gabe conducts his band-mates through half-a-dozen songs, full of abrupt changes, stops, and signaling'). Says he was the original singer of Dead Cross (replaced by Mike Patton) and Cattle Decapitation's originator.
